chapter: Chicago and New York with Louis Armstrong, 1925-30
title: The Nest's clientele and splitting the tips three ways
summary: The Nest drew society and big-time pimps; the three-man band split large tips evenly, Zutty bringing home piles of cash. Carrington was last seen in Washington in 1946.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: But this (nest) was a place where a lot of society worked, you know, for them big time acts that were playing in town and all. They came there you know? And as I said before, no blacks can go
there much other than the big time pimps.
Yes, that's right. I've seen this Merryl McCormick......
Millionaires used to go there. Slumming you know?
Was it white only or not?
Not it wasn't white only but the average........
They hired a black one after hours but they had to work.
It was an expensive place?
Yes it was kind of expensive.
(unintelligible)
you know, after all these people didn't work during the day.
The guys could afford that... the pimps you know?)?
Yes.
Big time guys.

Zutty said he made seventeen dollars tips you know at the Kelly Stable. Shoot, they used to make 50, 75 dollars each a night tips. I'm telling you, Zutty used to come home with so much money. I mean, it was split down between the orchestra. I mean
between the band.
Well you mean the three of you?
Yes.
Yes, the three of us.

And Jimmy Noon was the leader but he gave them just what he took of the tips, it was split even. And Zutty would come home and just put the money down. He hadn't even counted it. Just put it down over there because he was so tired.
Yes, I bet you were.
And I would count it and tell him how much he had made you know in tips.
What happened to Jerome Carrington?
Jerome Carrington the last time we saw him was in Washington DC. He was playing at the Rose Bud. Right, a block from the Ohio Theater, upstairs.
How long ago was that?
That was in '46. Because you were with the Slim Gaililard trio and I came out, I never forget that because you'd been gone so long, I came out to join you.
That's right.
For a while. That was in '46.
